name: Sub-cortical Nodular Heterotopia
aliases: Nodular Heterotopia of the Subcortical White Matter

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Sub-cortical Nodular Heterotopia

criteria.description: Presence of nodular gray matter heterotopia located in the subcortical white matter on brain MRI
History of focal epilepsy or seizure disorder consistent with heterotopia localization
Identification of pathogenic variants in FLNA gene or other associated genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic MRI findings plus clinical evidence of epilepsy or seizure disorder
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis primarily relies on neuroimaging and clinical presentation.

searchTerms: abnormal opening at base of skull
EEG shows slow waves in one area
focal slowing on brain wave test
localized slow brain activity on EEG
problems in brain movement control area

imaging: MRI showing nodular clusters of gray matter within the subcortical white matter
Absence of normal cortical lamination in affected areas
genetic: Pathogenic variants in FLNA gene (X-linked dominant inheritance)
Other rare gene mutations associated with neuronal migration defects
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing focal epileptiform discharges correlating with heterotopia location

distinguishingFeatures: Nodules located along the lateral ventricles rather than subcortical white matter
Typically associated with FLNA mutations but different clinical presentation
Smooth brain surface with absent or reduced gyri
More severe developmental delay and global neurological impairment

redFlags: Onset of drug-resistant focal seizures in early childhood
Sudden onset of focal neurological deficits
references: Guerrini R, Dobyns WB. Malformations of cortical development: clinical features and genetic causes. Lancet Neurol. 2014;13(7):710-726.
Sheen VL, et al. Filamin A mutations cause periventricular nodular heterotopia in humans. Nat Genet. 2001;29(2):117-121.
Barkovich AJ, et al. A developmental and genetic classification for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012;79(10):1035-1044.
